rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a blastocyst and acknowledges single-image limits, but it overstates confidence in a 3AA appearance; the ICM is not sharply compact and TE cohesion is only partly appreciable on this image.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, endometriosis, prior ectopic, semen, endometrium, and lifestyle with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with probability adjusted for favorable age and embryo quality versus endometriosis/ectopic risk; minor overreach around prior implantation evidence and some speculative modifiers.

Recommendations are largely evidence-based and consistent with IVF practice, especially SET and ectopic surveillance; slight deviations include somewhat broad discussion of diet/BMI and optional PGT-A framing in a very young patient.
Provides clear practical next steps for current transfer, ectopic monitoring, tubal evaluation, luteal support, and contingency planning if unsuccessful.
